concept.name: B-Tree vs. LSM-Tree Storage Engines

reviewRecord.reviewNotes: Approved canonical concept synthesized from 0 legacy articles and blogs.

concept.tagline: Comparing in-place mutable page trees (B+Trees) against append-only MemTable + SSTable compaction engines (LSM-Trees).
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of storage engine internals—from page splits and WAL to leveled/size-tiered compaction, Bloom filters, and the RUM conjecture.

spark.summary: B-Trees update fixed-size disk pages (4-16 KiB) in place for fast, predictable point and range reads, whereas LSM-Trees buffer writes sequentially in memory (MemTable + WAL) and merge immutable sorted runs (SSTables) in the background for orders-of-magnitude higher write throughput.
spark.keyTakeaway: B-Trees optimize read latency and predictability at the cost of random-write amplification, while LSM-Trees maximize sequential write throughput at the cost of background compaction I/O and multi-level read amplification.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Storage engines bridge volatile RAM and persistent block storage (NVMe/SSD).

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts B+Tree Mutable Page Lookup vs. LSM-Tree MemTable/SSTable Hierarchy (Root / MemTable -> Internal / L0 SST -> L1..Ln SSTables -> Leaf 8-16KiB); WAL + MemTable -> Immutable L0 -> Leveled Compaction (PUT(user:4812) -> Immutable MemTable -> L0 -> L1 Compaction -> vLog / Titan (opt)); Multi-Raft Consensus -> RocksDB LSM + Bloom + Block Cache (Multi-Raft Leader -> RocksDB / Pebble -> Titan vLog (SSD)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Compare page unit, read/write amplification, and compaction behavior across the three dominant disk-backed index families. Distributed NewSQL/KV engines like **TiKV** and **CockroachDB** (Pebble) run an LSM-Tree per node underneath **Multi-Raft** consensus groups.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore LSM storage design, Cassandra tombstone scans, and B-Tree index invalidation.

learningJourney.title: What are B-Trees and LSM-Trees
learningJourney.explanation:
Storage engines bridge volatile RAM and persistent block storage (NVMe/SSD). A **B+Tree** (8 KiB pages in PostgreSQL, 16 KiB in InnoDB) organizes keys in mutable, fixed-size pages linked in sorted order; with height 3–4 for 1B+ rows, internal nodes stay cached in RAM so point lookups need at most 1–2 disk reads.

A **Log-Structured Merge-Tree (LSM-Tree)** (RocksDB, Cassandra, Pebble) never mutates on-disk blocks in place. Writes append to a sequential WAL and an in-memory skiplist (`MemTable`), flushing immutable sorted `SSTables` (~64 MiB) to disk and merging them asynchronously in the background.

sectionDiagram.title: B+Tree Mutable Page Lookup vs. LSM-Tree MemTable/SSTable Hierarchy

cards.label: B+Tree Read Path
cards.detail: Traverses 3-4 cached internal pages to a single mutable leaf page (predictable p99).

cards.label: LSM Write Path
cards.detail: Appends sequentially to WAL + MemTable; zero random page rewrites on the hot path.

cards.label: Bloom Filter Guard
cards.detail: 10 bits/key (~1% FP) lets LSM point reads skip SSTables that do not contain the key.

sectionDiagram.summary: B+Trees pay random-write amplification for 1-lookup reads; LSM-Trees batch sequential writes and pay background compaction.

learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how B-Trees and LSM-Trees works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why we need LSM-Trees (and the RUM Conjecture trade-offs)
learningJourney.explanation:
Under heavy random-key `INSERT`/`UPDATE` workloads (time-series, IoT, write-heavy KV), B+Trees suffer **10x–30x+ write amplification** because modifying 100 bytes dirties an entire 8–16 KiB page (plus full-page WAL writes).

However, the **RUM Conjecture** proves you cannot minimize Read, Update/Write, and Memory/Space overhead simultaneously. LSM-Trees face two signature failure modes: **L0 Compaction Stalls** (hitting `level0_stop_writes_trigger`, default 36 in RocksDB, freezes all writes) and **Tombstone Scan Degradation** on range queries over deleted keys.

sectionDiagram.title: WAL + MemTable -> Immutable L0 -> Leveled Compaction

cards.label: Sequential I/O
cards.detail: Writes never seek random B-Tree leaf pages; MemTable flushes sequentially.

cards.label: Write-Stall Risk
cards.detail: If background compaction falls behind L0 flushes, RocksDB throttles or stops foreground writes.

cards.label: WiscKey / Titan
cards.detail: Separating large values (>1 KiB) into an append-only vLog cuts compaction write amplification sharply.

sectionDiagram.summary: LSM-Trees convert random writes into sequential flushes, but compaction bandwidth must keep pace with ingestion.

ideas.title: PostgreSQL Checkpoint Storms
ideas.description: In B-Trees, flushing thousands of dirty buffer-pool pages saturates NVMe queues unless checkpoint_completion_target is tuned (e.g. 0.9).

ideas.title: B-epsilon Trees
ideas.description: Hybrid B-epsilon trees attach small write buffers to internal B-Tree nodes to batch writes while preserving fast range scans.

learningJourney.title: Where B-Trees and LSM-Trees belong
learningJourney.explanation: Match the storage engine to your read/write ratio, range-scan frequency, and latency SLA.

benefits: Predictable point & range read latency; strong in-place MVCC/row-lock semantics for OLTP.
costs: High random-write amplification (10-30x+) and page fragmentation under heavy random inserts.

benefits: High write throughput, ~10x space amplification control, fast point reads with Bloom filters.
costs: Higher compaction write amplification than Size-Tiered; L0 stalls if compaction lags.

benefits: Lowest write amplification for append-heavy time-series and logging workloads.
costs: Up to 50% temporary disk space overhead during major compactions; slower point/range reads.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How Compaction, Bloom Filters, and Checkpoints are tuned
learningJourney.explanation:
Tune each engine around its bottleneck:

1. **LSM-Tree**: Size `bits_per_key = 10` (~1% false positive Bloom filter), pin L0/L1 index & filter blocks in block cache, and dedicate enough background compaction threads (`max_background_jobs`) so `L0` never hits `level0_stop_writes_trigger`.
2. **B+Tree**: Keep working set in `shared_buffers` / `innodb_buffer_pool_size` (~70-80% RAM), set `checkpoint_completion_target = 0.9`, and use k-ordered primary keys (UUIDv7 / Snowflake) instead of random UUIDv4 to eliminate page splits.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: B+Tree vs. Leveled LSM vs. Size-Tiered LSM
learningJourney.explanation: Compare page unit, read/write amplification, and compaction behavior across the three dominant disk-backed index families.

benefits: 1-2 IOs on cold point reads; zero compaction stalls; fast ordered range scans.
costs: Random-write amplification and B-Tree page splits on random UUID keys.

benefits: Disjoint key ranges per level L1+; low space amplification (~1.1x) and good read p99.
costs: 10-30x compaction write amplification as levels merge repeatedly.

benefits: Lowest write amplification; ideal for write-once immutable time-series.
costs: High read amplification and 2x disk headroom required for major compaction.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production example: Distributed KV Store (Multi-Raft + RocksDB + Titan)
learningJourney.explanation: Distributed NewSQL/KV engines like **TiKV** and **CockroachDB** (Pebble) run an LSM-Tree per node underneath **Multi-Raft** consensus groups. Separating large values (>1 KiB) into an append-only **Titan/vLog** keeps the LSM key-index compact in RAM while bounding compaction I/O.

sectionDiagram.title: Multi-Raft Consensus -> RocksDB LSM + Bloom + Block Cache

cards.label: Write-Group Batching
cards.detail: Coalesces concurrent Raft commits into a single RocksDB WriteBatch + fsync.

cards.label: Block Cache Pinning
cards.detail: Pin L0/L1 filter and index blocks in RAM so point reads avoid extra SSD seeks.

cards.label: Rate-Limited Compaction
cards.detail: Cap compaction MB/s so background merges never starve foreground read tail latency.

sectionDiagram.summary: Pairing Multi-Raft with rate-limited RocksDB compaction delivers linearizable writes and predictable reads.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why does inserting random UUIDv4 primary keys into a large PostgreSQL or InnoDB B+Tree table degrade write throughput far more than inserting monotonic UUIDv7 / Snowflake IDs?

options.text: Random keys scatter across cold leaf pages, causing buffer-pool cache misses, page splits, and 10-30x random-write amplification
options.feedback: Correct: monotonic keys append to the rightmost leaf page (staying hot in RAM), whereas random keys dirty pages across the entire tree.
WAL is always active; the bottleneck is random leaf-page I/O and splits.
B+Trees store 128-bit UUIDs natively; only key ordering affects page locality.

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
